notes: SHIP v1.14.439 - A DOOR THAT COMES HOME MUST ALSO COME BACK HOME. THE DEFECT, LIVE AT .438. .438 moved ASSIGN, QR and LOG NOTE into Build so a technician could act on the rack in front of them without leaving the operational centre. deploy_assignRack's own tail still ended with deploy_showRackDetail(deployId, rackId), so tapping Assign in Build saved the assignment, toasted, and then navigated the technician out of Build and onto the rack detail - the exact surface the merge exists to retire. Same wrong-landing shape as .436, shipped one ship after .436 fixed it, by the ship that moved the control. QR and LOG NOTE were checked and are clean: neither re-renders anything on completion. HOW IT WAS FOUND, because the method matters more than the fix. It was not found by tapping the button. It was found while inventorying the refresh coupling for merge step 3b, by asking a different question than the plan asked: not what does the phase-card block contain, but which code assumes the surface it refreshes is the rack detail. The answer is THIRTEEN call sites, and step 3a had recorded FOUR. The other nine are outside the block 3b was scoped to lift - four resume after a modal (ge_captureSkip, ge_captureSave, ge_onCompleteTap's rack-missing fallback, ta_resolveUnblock) and five are emitted INSIDE the card markup by checklist_addItem, checklist_removeItem, checklist_renameItem, checklist_toggleEdit and deploy_flagPhaseReverify. A hardcoded destination is invisible for exactly as long as there is only one destination. THE FIX IS A DISPATCHER, NOT A CALLBACK. phase_refreshSurface(surface, deployId, rackId) routes 'build' to bw_render and everything else to deploy_showRackDetail. The key is a STRING on purpose: four of the thirteen sites resume after a modal and five more are emitted into onclick attributes, so the calling scope is long gone by the time the refresh runs. A string survives an onclick attribute and a stored context object; a closure survives neither. This is also the foundation merge step 3b needs, which is why it lands as its own small ship instead of inside a large one. BYTE-IDENTICAL BY DEFAULT. surface is optional and omitting it means 'detail'. The rack detail's own ASSIGN button passes two arguments exactly as it did at .438, so every pre-.439 caller behaves as shipped - pinned by a test that calls the door with no surface and asserts Build does NOT re-render. CONTRACT 14. An unknown surface key console.warns and still refreshes the detail rather than landing the technician nowhere; if bw_render is missing it says so and falls back. No silent path. ARITY DISCIPLINE. Build's action table now carries the surface as a third element, and QR and LOG NOTE - which have no refresh tail - are still called at their declared two-argument arity rather than handed an argument they never read. TESTS: 27-rack-capabilities-in-build grows from five to eight. ASSIGN from Build re-renders Build and lands on the detail ZERO times; a caller naming no surface refreshes the detail and never Build; an unknown key warns and still lands somewhere. The detail assertion is exact and not a bound - the defect value is 1 and a less-than-or-equal-to-1 would have admitted it, which is the failure mode that hid the .427 aisle defect for months. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, CSS braces balanced, CRLF intact, three-stamp lockstep. No CSS change, no renderer change - consolidation remains stopped per owner directive. DEVICE-VERIFY: open BUILD with an active rack and tap ASSIGN. Enter a name and confirm. PASS is the assignment saving and BUILD still being the screen you are looking at. FAIL is landing on the rack detail.
